title: Gravity filtration of environmental DNA: A simple, fast, and power-free method
author: Oka, Miya, et al.

steps.title: Sterilize all reusable components
steps.instruction: Immerse the 3D‑printed connecting attachment, the cut‑off pipette‑tip adjuster, and the plastic tube in 10 % commercial bleach (≈0.6 % NaOCl) for at least 5 min, then rinse with sterile water and let air‑dry.

steps.title: Print or obtain the attachment
steps.instruction: If not already available, print the attachment using a stereolithography 3‑D printer (e.g., ELEGOO Mars Pro 2) with Fusion 360 CAD files; production rate is ~12 pieces per 3 h and resin cost < 0.5 USD each.

steps.title: Assemble the gravity‑filtration unit
steps.instruction: Connect the sterilized 3‑D‑printed attachment to the 1 L airtight plastic bag (DP16‑TN1000, COWPACK LTD). Attach the Sterivex filter cartridge (0.45 µm pore size, Merck Millipore) to the attachment. Fit a plastic tube (inner diameter 4 mm) with the cut‑off 10 µL pipette‑tip base onto the cartridge outlet, ensuring all joints are tight to prevent air leaks. (Alternatively, a 3 mm‑ID tube may be attached directly without the adjuster.)

steps.title: Prepare the sample bag
steps.instruction: Fill the sealed 1 L plastic bag with the water sample to be filtered (e.g., seawater, brackish water, freshwater, or pond water).

steps.title: Create air‑inlet hole in the bag
steps.instruction: Pierce a small hole in the upper part of the hanging bag to allow air influx and avoid negative pressure that would slow filtration.

steps.title: Hang the system at the desired height
steps.instruction: Suspend the assembled unit from a support so that the bag is positioned 2 m–9 m above the ground; heights up to ~2 m are easily manageable in the field, while 9 m gives filtration speed comparable to a vacuum aspirator.

steps.title: Run gravity filtration
steps.instruction: Allow the water to flow by gravity through the Sterivex filter and out the plastic tube. Filtration of 1 L typically completes in 10–60 min depending on height and water turbidity. For very turbid pond water, record the volume filtered after 2 h if complete filtration is not achieved.

steps.title: Disassemble and store filter cartridge
steps.instruction: After filtration, detach the Sterivex cartridge, cap it, and store it at –20 °C or process it immediately for eDNA extraction according to standard metabarcoding protocols.

steps.title: Optional performance validation
steps.instruction: To assess filtration speed, repeat the procedure at heights of 2 m, 4 m, and 9 m using three replicates per condition. Measure the time required to filter 1 L of each water type (seawater, brackish water, freshwater). For pond water, record the amount filtered in 2 h. Note that at 2 m, seawater and brackish water filter in ~10 min and ~17 min respectively, while turbid freshwater may require impractically long times.
